result:
I’ll trace prompt caching and invalidation, apply the repository’s Python conventions, and add focused tests for registry isolation and failed updates.
The cache keys omit the registry URI, and all invalidation paths use those shared keys. I’ll add the client’s resolved registry URI to cache keys and invalidation calls. Invalidation already follows successful mutations; tests will verify that failures preserve cached entries.
The version and alias isolation tests pass, including cache reuse by separate clients on the same registry. I’m finishing the mutation tests and checking implicit registry resolution. The first run also hit an inherited OpenTelemetry setting that breaks tracing setup; I’ll unset it for the test command.
All 54 selected tests passed, with six unsupported FileStore cases skipped. Coverage includes registry resolution, version and alias isolation, same-registry reuse, TTL behavior, and successful and failed mutations. Pytest then hit a sandbox permission error in its process-reporting summary hook.
Prompt cache keys and invalidation now include the client’s resolved registry URI, preventing cross-registry collisions for versions and aliases. TTL and same-registry reuse remain unchanged; failed mutations preserve cached entries.

Added regression coverage: 54 tests passed, six skipped. Pytest’s final reporting hook encountered a sandbox permission error after tests completed. No dependencies installed.
